content.text: The blockchain does not have a map of restricted countries. A wallet address in Lagos processes a transaction identically to one in London. USDT moves from a buyer in Manila to a seller in Harare in under 60 seconds — no correspondent bank, no SWIFT delay, no compliance officer deciding whether the corridor is permitted. This is the operational reality that creators across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, Cameroon, Tanzania, and the Philippines are using right now to sell [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-stores-kyc-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-options-ethiopian-digital-creators-what-nobody-tells-3|COREMERCH guide to payment]]s-explained-digital-creators-7|Digital Product]] products to a global audience. The [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-2|infrastructure]] exists. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages serves the storefront. NOWPayments verifies the payment on-chain and fires a webhook automatically. The product delivers before the buyer closes their wallet. The only question is whether you have assembled the stack correctly.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What You Can Actually Get Done Today

You can start by deploying a minimum viable stack that allows you to sell digital products and accept payments without relying on Stripe or PayPal. This stack can be built using free and open-source tools like GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and Supabase. By leveraging these tools, you can create a fully functional online store with automatic crypto payment processing and instant product delivery.
The Minimum Viable Stack That Works

The minimum viable stack consists of a hosting platform, a backend logic provider, an order storage solution, and a payment processing system. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages can be used for hosting, while Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script can handle backend logic. Supabase or Google Sheets can store orders, and NOWPayments can process crypto payments with a 0.5% fee.
Skipping the Steps That Do Not Matter Yet

Cloudflare Pages and GitHub Pages both provide free static site hosting that works identically regardless of where the store operator is located. A store deployed on Cloudflare Pages by a creator in Harare is served from Cloudflare's global edge network — the same infrastructure that serves enterprises in New York. Neither platform imposes geographic restrictions on who can deploy a store or who can access it. Combined with NOWPayments for payment processing and Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, this creates a complete commerce infrastructure with zero hosting costs and no geographic restrictions at any layer of the stack.
Deploy your minimum viable stack today.
Getting Your First Transaction Live

Creators in Ethiopia, Cameroon, Tanzania, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, and the Philippines face a compounded challenge: not only are conventional payment platforms unavailable, but local banking infrastructure may add additional friction to receiving international transfers through alternative channels. Crypto payments remove this layer entirely. A seller in Addis Ababa and a seller in Amsterdam receive USDT transactions through the same NOWPayments infrastructure, at the same speed, with the same 0.5% fee. The blockchain has no knowledge of which country a wallet is located in. The webhook fires to both backends identically. Geographic neutrality is not a feature — it is the fundamental property of how blockchains work.
What to Do in the Next 24 Hours

In the next 24 hours, you should focus on deploying your minimum viable stack and getting your first transaction live. This involves setting up your hosting platform, configuring your backend logic, and integrating your payment processing system. By taking these steps, you can establish a sovereign commerce infrastructure that allows you to sell digital products and reach a global audience without relying on Stripe or PayPal.
